points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 亚当·斯密出生于苏格兰法夫郡的柯科迪，是海关官员亚当·斯密和玛格丽特道格拉斯的儿子。他从小展现出非凡的智力，据说在四岁时被吉普赛人短暂拐走，九岁时已能阅读复杂的文学作品。这段时期的教育为他后来的学术成就奠定了基础，特别是他对古典文学和哲学的早期接触，塑造了他独特的思维方式。
points.descriptionEn: Adam Smith was born in Kirkcaldy, Fife, Scotland, to Adam Smith, a customs official, and Margaret Douglas. He displayed exceptional intelligence from an early age, reportedly being briefly kidnapped by gypsies at age four and reading complex literary works by age nine. This period of education laid the foundation for his later academic achievements, particularly his early exposure to classical literature and philosophy, which shaped his unique way of thinking.

points.title: 大学教育
points.description: 斯密进入格拉斯哥大学学习，师从著名哲学家弗朗西斯·哈奇森。在这里，他接触到道德哲学、政治经济学和古典文学，并展现出卓越的学术才能。1740年，他获得牛津大学贝利学院的奖学金，但这段牛津经历并不愉快，他后来批评牛津的教学方法陈旧且缺乏活力。格拉斯哥大学的经历对他影响深远，形成了他后来思想体系的基础。
points.descriptionEn: Smith attended the University of Glasgow, where he studied under the renowned philosopher Francis Hutcheson. Here, he was exposed to moral philosophy, political economy, and classical literature, demonstrating exceptional academic abilities. In 1740, he received a Snell Exhibition to Balliol College, Oxford, but his Oxford experience was unpleasant, and he later criticized the university's outdated teaching methods. His time at Glasgow profoundly influenced him, forming the foundation of his later philosophical system.

points.title: 学术起步
points.description: 斯密回到爱丁堡，开始他的学术生涯。他最初在爱丁堡大学担任修辞学和文学讲师，逐渐建立起学术声誉。这一时期，他开始系统思考经济和社会问题，并结识了大卫·休谟等苏格兰启蒙运动的重要人物。这些思想交流对他的学术发展产生了深远影响，为他后来的著作奠定了思想基础。1751年，他接受格拉斯哥大学的邀请，担任逻辑学教授，随后转任道德哲学教授。
points.descriptionEn: Smith returned to Edinburgh and began his academic career. Initially, he lectured on rhetoric and literature at the University of Edinburgh, gradually building his academic reputation. During this period, he began systematically contemplating economic and social issues and met key figures of the Scottish Enlightenment such as David Hume. These intellectual exchanges profoundly influenced his academic development, laying the philosophical groundwork for his later works. In 1751, he accepted an invitation to the University of Glasgow, becoming Professor of Logic and later Moral Philosophy.

points.title: 学术巅峰
points.description: 在格拉斯哥大学担任道德哲学教授期间，斯密完成了他第一部重要著作《道德情操论》(1759)。这部作品探讨了人类道德行为的心理基础，提出了著名的'旁观者'理论，为他后来的经济学思想奠定了哲学基础。作为道德哲学教授，他的课程涵盖伦理学、法学、政治学和经济学，这些内容后来都融入了他的主要著作中。1763年，他获得格拉斯哥大学授予的法学博士学位，并开始为年轻的巴克公爵担任私人导师，这为他后来的欧洲之行创造了条件。
points.descriptionEn: During his tenure as Professor of Moral Philosophy at the University of Glasgow, Smith completed his first major work, 'The Theory of Moral Sentiments' (1759). This work explored the psychological foundations of human moral behavior, introducing his famous concept of the 'impartial spectator,' which laid the philosophical groundwork for his later economic ideas. As a moral philosophy professor, his courses covered ethics, jurisprudence, politics, and economics—subjects that would later be incorporated into his major works. In 1763, he was awarded a Doctor of Laws degree from Glasgow University and began tutoring the young Duke of Buccleuch, which created the opportunity for his subsequent European tour.

points.title: 欧洲之行
points.description: 斯密作为巴克公爵的导师，陪同他前往欧洲大陆，在法国图卢兹停留两年，后移居巴黎。在巴黎，他与伏尔泰、魁奈、杜尔哥等法国启蒙思想家和经济学家密切交往，深入了解法国的经济和社会状况。这段经历极大地丰富了他的思想，特别是对重农学派经济理论的研究。1766年回到英国后，他专注于写作，最终在1776年出版了改变世界的著作《国富论》，这部作品系统地阐述了自由市场经济理论，成为现代资本主义的理论基础。
points.descriptionEn: As tutor to the Duke of Buccleuch, Smith accompanied him on a tour of continental Europe, spending two years in Toulouse, France, before moving to Paris. In Paris, he closely interacted with French Enlightenment thinkers and economists such as Voltaire, François Quesnay, and Anne-Robert-Jacques Turgot, gaining deep insights into French economic and social conditions. This experience greatly enriched his thinking, particularly his study of Physiocratic economic theory. After returning to Britain in 1766, he focused on writing, ultimately publishing his world-changing work 'An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations' in 1776, which systematically articulated the theory of free-market economics and became the theoretical foundation of modern capitalism.

supporter.zh: 亚当·斯密被誉为现代经济学之父，他的自由市场理论为资本主义经济体系奠定了理论基础。支持者认为他提出的'看不见的手'概念揭示了市场自我调节的机制，主张自由竞争和有限政府干预，促进了经济繁荣和个人自由。他的思想不仅影响了经济学发展，还对政治哲学、法律和社会制度产生了深远影响，成为启蒙运动的核心思想之一。
supporter.en: Adam Smith is hailed as the father of modern economics, and his free-market theory laid the theoretical foundation for capitalist economic systems. Supporters argue that his concept of the 'invisible hand' reveals the self-regulating mechanism of markets, advocating for free competition and limited government intervention, which promotes economic prosperity and individual freedom. His ideas have not only influenced economic development but also had profound impacts on political philosophy, law, and social institutions, becoming one of the core ideas of the Enlightenment.

critic.zh: 批评者指出斯密的理论存在明显局限性，他忽视了市场失灵、外部性和信息不对称等问题，过度理想化了市场机制。他的理论未能充分考虑到社会不平等、环境破坏和公共产品供给不足等现实问题。此外，斯密对殖民主义的辩护和对工人阶级处境的忽视也受到批评。现代经济学研究表明，纯粹的自由市场并不能解决所有经济问题，需要适当的政府干预和监管。
critic.en: Critics point out that Smith's theory has significant limitations, as he ignored market failures, externalities, and information asymmetries, overly idealizing market mechanisms. His theories failed to adequately address real-world issues such as social inequality, environmental degradation, and insufficient provision of public goods. Additionally, Smith's defense of colonialism and his neglect of the working class's situation have been criticized. Modern economic research shows that pure free markets cannot solve all economic problems and require appropriate government intervention and regulation.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，亚当·斯密被定位为苏格兰启蒙运动的关键人物，他的思想体系融合了哲学、伦理学和经济学。历史学者认为，斯密的理论并非简单的自由放任，而是强调在适当的制度框架下市场与政府的平衡。在流行文化中，斯密常被简化为'看不见的手'的提出者，成为资本主义象征，但这种简化忽视了他思想的复杂性和对道德哲学的重视。他的著作至今仍是经济学和政治哲学研究的基础文本，持续影响着当代经济政策制定。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Adam Smith is positioned as a key figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, whose intellectual system integrated philosophy, ethics, and economics. Historians argue that Smith's theory was not simply about laissez-faire but emphasized the balance between markets and government within appropriate institutional frameworks. In popular culture, Smith is often simplified as the proponent of the 'invisible hand' and a symbol of capitalism, but this simplification overlooks the complexity of his thought and his emphasis on moral philosophy. His works remain foundational texts in economics and political philosophy, continuing to influence contemporary economic policy-making.

self.zh: 我们每天所需要的食物和饮料，不是出自屠户、酿酒师或面包师的恩惠，而是出自他们自利的打算。
self.en: It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest.

others.zh: 亚当·斯密是历史上最伟大的经济学家，他的《国富论》是经济学领域的里程碑，为现代资本主义提供了理论基础。
others.en: Adam Smith was the greatest economist in history, and his 'Wealth of Nations' is a milestone in the field of economics, providing the theoretical foundation for modern capitalism.
